use: 'Yurushite' (forgive me) and 'Zettai yurusanai' (I'll never forgive you) are the everyday uses.

example.ja: もう怒ってないよ、許してあげる。
example.english: I'm not mad anymore. I forgive you.

examplePolite.ja: もう怒っていません。許しますよ。
examplePolite.english: I'm not angry anymore. I forgive you.

notes: The 'allow' sense is mostly formal, as in 'jikan ga yuruseba' (if time allows).

use: Mostly in apologies on arrival: 'Omatase!' or 'Matasete gomen'.

example.ja: ごめんね、長いこと待たせちゃって。
example.english: Sorry for keeping you waiting so long.

examplePolite.romaji: Nagai koto omatase shite, sumimasen deshita.
examplePolite.ja: 長いことお待たせして、すみませんでした。
examplePolite.english: I'm sorry for keeping you waiting so long.

notes: The causative of matsu (wait). Staff say 'Omatase shimashita' when they bring your order.

english: hold back (out of politeness); politely decline
use: 'Enryo shinaide' means 'Don't be shy, help yourself'; 'Enryo shimasu' politely turns something down.

example.ja: 遠慮しないで、たくさん食べてね。
example.english: Don't be shy, eat as much as you like.

examplePolite.romaji: Enryo shinaide, takusan tabete kudasai ne.
examplePolite.ja: 遠慮しないで、たくさん食べてくださいね。
examplePolite.english: Don't be shy, please eat as much as you like.

notes: 'Goenryo kudasai' on signs means 'please refrain', as with smoking or photos.

english: give up (a seat, a turn); hand over
use: The classic use is giving up your seat on a train: 'seki o yuzuru'.

example.romaji: Obaachan ni seki o yuzutta yo.
example.ja: おばあちゃんに席を譲ったよ。
example.english: I gave my seat to an old lady.

examplePolite.ja: おばあさんに席を譲りました。
examplePolite.english: I gave my seat to an old lady.

notes: Also letting someone go first, or passing something on to them.

use: Often after -te mo: 'Tsukatte mo kamawanai yo' (You're welcome to use it).

examplePolite.ja: 明日でも構いませんよ。

notes: In casual talk, 'ii yo' is more common; kamawanai sounds a little firmer.

use: The thing noticed takes ni: 'Machigai ni kizuita' (I noticed the mistake).

example.ja: ごめん、全然気付かなかったよ。
example.english: Sorry, I didn't notice at all.

examplePolite.ja: すみません、全然気付きませんでした。
examplePolite.english: Sorry, I didn't notice at all.

notes: Also written 気づく; ki ga tsuku means the same.

english: think of, come up with (an idea)
use: For an idea popping into your head: 'Ii koto omoitsuita!' (I've got a great idea!).

example.ja: 何かいいアイデア思いついた？
example.english: Have you thought of any good ideas?

examplePolite.romaji: Nanika ii aidea o omoitsukimashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: 何かいいアイデアを思いつきましたか？
examplePolite.english: Have you thought of any good ideas?

notes: Omoidasu (remember) sounds close: omoitsuku is a new thought, omoidasu an old one.

use: Common in 'yosou yori' (than expected), 'yosou doori' (as expected) and 'yosou gai' (unexpected).

example.romaji: Kore, yosou yori zutto oishii ne.
example.ja: これ、予想よりずっとおいしいね。
example.english: This is way tastier than I expected.

examplePolite.romaji: Kore, yosou yori zutto oishii desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: これ、予想よりずっとおいしいですね。
examplePolite.english: This is much tastier than I expected.

notes: Also yosou suru (predict, guess), as with scores or results.

use: Usually about a belief that turns out to be wrong.

example.romaji: Kyou wa yasumi da to omoikondeta.
example.ja: 今日は休みだと思い込んでた。
example.english: I was sure today was a day off.

examplePolite.romaji: Kyou wa yasumi da to omoikonde imashita.
examplePolite.ja: 今日は休みだと思い込んでいました。
examplePolite.english: I was convinced today was a day off.

notes: The noun omoikomi means a mistaken belief or preconception.

use: Usually in -te iru: 'Ochikonderu' (She's feeling down). 'Ochikomanaide' means 'Don't let it get you down'.

example.romaji: Shiken ni ochite, ochikonderu n da.
example.ja: 試験に落ちて、落ち込んでるんだ。
example.english: I failed the exam, so I'm feeling down.

examplePolite.romaji: Shiken ni ochite, ochikonde iru n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 試験に落ちて、落ち込んでいるんです。
examplePolite.english: I failed the exam, so I'm feeling down.

use: Mostly emotional hurt from words or actions.

example.romaji: Sonna koto iwareru to kizutsuku yo.
example.ja: そんなこと言われると傷つくよ。
example.english: It hurts when you say things like that.

examplePolite.romaji: Sonna koto o iwareru to kizutsukimasu yo.
examplePolite.ja: そんなことを言われると傷つきますよ。
examplePolite.english: It hurts when you say things like that.

notes: Kizutsukeru is the other side: to hurt someone.

use: Said about the person or thing: 'Aitsu mukatsuku' (That guy pisses me off).

example.romaji: Ano hito no taido, maji mukatsuku.
example.ja: あの人の態度、マジムカつく。
example.english: That guy's attitude really pisses me off.

notes: Its original sense is feeling sick to the stomach. Softer: haradatsu or iraira suru.

use: Said about what makes you mad: 'Are, hontou ni haradatsu' (That really makes me mad).

example.ja: 今思い出しても腹立つ。
example.english: It still makes me mad just thinking about it.

examplePolite.romaji: Ima omoidashite mo hara ga tachimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 今思い出しても腹が立ちます。
examplePolite.english: It still makes me angry just thinking about it.

notes: Full form hara ga tatsu. Less crude than mukatsuku.

example.romaji: Aseranakute ii yo. Mada jikan aru kara.
example.ja: 焦らなくていいよ。まだ時間あるから。
example.english: No need to rush. There's still time.

examplePolite.romaji: Aseranakute ii desu yo. Mada jikan ga arimasu kara.
examplePolite.ja: 焦らなくていいですよ。まだ時間がありますから。
examplePolite.english: No need to rush. There's still time.

notes: It conjugates like kaeru (go home): aseranai, aserimasu, not asenai.

use: Awatete (in a rush) is the most common form; 'Awatenaide' means 'Don't panic'.

example.romaji: Nebou shite, awatete ie o deta.
example.ja: 寝坊して、慌てて家を出た。
example.english: I overslept and rushed out of the house.

examplePolite.romaji: Nebou shite, awatete ie o demashita.
examplePolite.ja: 寝坊して、慌てて家を出ました。
examplePolite.english: I overslept and rushed out of the house.

notes: Aseru is the pressure you feel inside; awateru is flustered, hurried action.

english: get scared, be startled; chicken out

example.romaji: Kyuu ni inu ga dete kite, bibitta yo.
example.ja: 急に犬が出てきて、ビビったよ。
example.english: A dog suddenly jumped out and scared me.

examplePolite.romaji: Kyuu ni inu ga dete kite, bibirimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 急に犬が出てきて、ビビりました。
examplePolite.english: A dog suddenly jumped out and gave me a fright.

notes: Bibiri is a scaredy-cat. Neutral words: odoroku (be surprised), kowai (scary).

english: let one's guard down, get careless
use: Mostly as a warning: 'Yudan suru na' (Don't let your guard down).

example.romaji: Saigo made yudan shicha dame da yo.
example.ja: 最後まで油断しちゃだめだよ。
example.english: Don't let your guard down until the very end.

examplePolite.romaji: Saigo made yudan shinaide kudasai ne.
examplePolite.ja: 最後まで油断しないでくださいね。
examplePolite.english: Please don't let your guard down until the very end.

notes: 'Yudan dekinai' means you have to stay on your toes around someone or something.
